recommended_approach: Use a Mantaflow **Gas (smoke/fire) simulation** with the standard workflow **Domain → Flow → (Effectors) → Bake**, then render the plume by assigning a **volume material on the Domain** that drives **blackbody fire emission from the simulation’s temperature/flame fields**. For shading, start with **Principled Volume** (physically-based volume shader) and use its built-in **Blackbody** controls, sourcing the volume grids via **Temperature Attribute (typically "temperature")** and density via **Density Attribute (typically "density")**; alternatively use the **Volume Info** node outputs (**Flame**, **Temperature**, **Density**) to build a custom emission/scatter setup.

mantaflow_workflow.bake_note: Save the .blend before baking; bake cache after setting up Domain/Flow/Effector and the Domain material.

principled_volume_node.color_attribute: color (typical color grid name for smoke)
principled_volume_node.temperature_attribute: temperature (typical temperature grid name for fire)
principled_volume_node.blackbody_intensity: Set to 1 for physically accurate intensity (per docs).

volume_info_node_outputs.density: Smoke density scalar from Fluid Domain
volume_info_node_outputs.flame: Fire (flame) scalar density from Fluid Domain (outputs are the same across its channels)
volume_info_node_outputs.temperature: 0–1 mapped to 0–1000 kelvin (per docs); often needs scaling/remapping for desired look

warnings: Mantaflow setup order matters: you need at least one Domain and one Flow, and the Domain must exist before baking.
Save the blend file before baking the cache (recommended in the documented workflow).
If using the Volume Info node for temperature-driven blackbody, note its Temperature output mapping: 0–1 corresponds to 0–1000 K (may require scaling/remapping for a convincing orange flame).
Principled Volume’s Blackbody Intensity is documented as physically accurate at 1; changing it will be an artistic override. ലക്ഷ
alternative_approaches: Instead of Principled Volume, build a custom volume shader using volume components (Volume Absorption/Scatter/Emission) and read simulation fields via Attribute/Volume Info (e.g., Temperature → Blackbody → Emission).
